segments.english: Peleg lived thirty years, and he fathered Reu.
segments.literal: and-lived Peleg thirty year and-fathered [object-marker] Reu

tokens.note: singular after a numeral above ten

grammar: וַיְחִי and וַיּוֹלֶד are wayyiqtols that carry the genealogy forward.
The etnaḥta on שָׁנָה divides the age from the birth of the son.
שָׁנָה is singular after שְׁלֹשִׁים, as Hebrew usually has it with tens.
segments.note: Plain formulaic verse; 'fathered' renders the Hifil of ילד.

commentary.summary: Targum Onkelos renders the verse closely: וַחֲיָא פֶלֶג תְּלָתִין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת רְעוּ, the same sense as the English.

segments.english: After he fathered Reu, Peleg lived two hundred nine years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
segments.literal: and-lived Peleg after fathering-him [object-marker] Reu nine years and-two-hundreds year and-fathered sons and-daughters

tokens.note: infinitive construct with 3rd masculine singular suffix: 'his fathering'

phrases.literal: 'nine years and-two-hundred year'; the smaller number comes first

phrases.english: and he fathered sons and daughters

grammar: The verse repeats the opening verb, then gives the time after the birth of Reu in a clause with an infinitive construct and suffix.
The number is given smaller unit first: 'nine years and two hundred year'.
The revia on פֶלֶג and zaqef qaton on רְעוּ mark the stages of the opening clause; the etnaḥta falls after the total.
The paragraph mark (ס) closes the entry.
segments.note: The English reorders the clause for readability; the Hebrew puts 'Peleg lived' first, then the time after the birth.

commentary.summary: Targum Onkelos: וַחֲיָא פֶלֶג בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת רְעוּ מָאתָן וּתְשַׁע שְׁנִין, the same sense, with the number in the same order.

segments.english: Reu lived thirty-two years, and he fathered Serug.
segments.literal: and-lived Reu two and-thirty year and-fathered [object-marker] Serug
grammar: The units come before the tens: 'two and thirty'.
The zaqef qaton on רְעוּ and the etnaḥta on שָׁנָה divide the verse.

commentary.summary: Targum Onkelos: וַחֲיָא רְעוּ תְּלָתִין וְתַרְתֵּין שְׁנִין וְאוֹלִיד יָת שְׂרוּג, the same sense.

segments.english: After he fathered Serug, Reu lived two hundred seven years, and he fathered sons and daughters.
segments.literal: and-lived Reu after fathering-him [object-marker] Serug seven years and-two-hundreds year and-fathered sons and-daughters

tokens.note: infinitive construct with 3rd masculine singular suffix: 'his fathering'

phrases.english: and he fathered sons and daughters

grammar: The verse has the same pattern as 11:19.
The revia on רְעוּ and zaqef qaton on שְׂרוּג divide the opening clause.
שֶׁבַע is the feminine form, agreeing with שָׁנִים, which is itself feminine in grammar though masculine in ending.
segments.note: The English reorders the clause for readability.

commentary.summary: Targum Onkelos: וַחֲיָא רְעוּ בָּתַר דְּאוֹלִיד יָת שְׂרוּג מָאתָן וּשְׁבַע שְׁנִין, the same sense.
